title: Get to Know the Workspace
metaDescription: Explore the JigsawDesigner canvas, toolbar and panels, see how selection changes the inspector, and find your way around the Mac and iPhone layouts.
intro: Find the canvas, toolbar and panels, understand what changes when you select an object, and compare the Mac and iPhone layouts.
captureNote: Screenshots show the English macOS development build. The iPhone examples were captured in the iOS Simulator.
workspaceIntro: Draw and refine your design in the center, with tools above and the relevant controls on either side.
workspaceSidebar: Switch between tools, layers and templates in the left sidebar.
workspaceNote: If you cannot see the generation settings, use Select and click an empty area of the canvas, or choose Deselect All in the Tools panel.
toolsIntro: Choose a tool to see its real toolbar button, the gesture and the finished result. Keyboard shortcuts refer to the Mac editor.
parametersTitle: Set the canvas and generation parameters
parametersIntro: With nothing selected, the right inspector shows settings for the whole project. The values in this example are not recommended defaults.
gridText: Grid Size controls the generator's subdivision. It is separate from the spacing of the visible editor grid.
piecesText: Piece Count sets the requested number of pieces. The contour and generation conditions can change the final count.
slotText: Slot Min / Max Distance defines which edge lengths can receive a slot. Edges outside that range remain straight. These values are not cutting kerf or a gap between pieces.
parametersNote: Canvas sizes are in pixels. Check the physical size in your production software. Shape Count counts top-level objects, not finished puzzle pieces.
inspectorTitle: Select an object to refine its properties
inspectorIntro: The inspector changes with your selection. Adjust the selected object's position, dimensions, rotation and appearance.
styleText: Set a solid fill, stroke color and line width. Some complex fills and gradients are read-only.
inspectorNote: Object dimensions describe the selection, not the entire canvas. Lock proportions when you want to preserve its shape while resizing.
templatesTitle: Find a connection style in the template library
templatesIntro: Slot templates define the curve along a connection. Explore the library, then create a version of your own.
templatesNote: Built-in templates cannot be overwritten or deleted. A highlighted template does not mean every generated edge uses that one shape; inspect the result with your chosen contour and parameters.
workflowTitle: Create your own slot template in four steps
workflowIntro: Follow the same Website Demo Wave example from an empty editor to a saved custom template.
step1Text: Click + in Templates and enter a name. Save becomes available when the template has a name and a valid path.
step2Text: Draw an open Bézier curve, then choose Edit Points. Move anchors to position the path and drag the hollow handles to shape its bends.
step3Text: Choose Finish Editing, inspect the curve, then Save. Path Dimensions describes the curve's bounding box, not the size of a finished puzzle piece.
step4Text: Back in Templates, search for Website Demo. The matching custom template card confirms it is saved. Select it and try it on a simple closed contour.
workflowNote: Import SVG can provide a starting path. The template editor reads the first supported path, so prepare an SVG containing the curve you want to use.
layersTitle: Find the path, then refine its nodes
layersIntro: Generated artwork remains editable. Use the layer tree to locate a path, then adjust its anchors and handles on the canvas.
selectLayerText: Click a layer row to select its object. The highlighted row and canvas selection stay connected.
anchorsText: Select the path and switch to Point Edit. Drag a filled anchor to change where the path passes.
handlesText: Select a curve anchor to reveal its hollow control handles. Drag a handle to change the curve's direction and bend.
layersNote: The detailed artwork demonstrates nested layers; the simple curve makes anchors and handles easier to see. They are separate teaching examples. A parent's lock or visibility setting also affects its children.
advancedIntro: These three views show different parts of the same Advanced Settings window: editor controls, pencil options, and export and saving.
pencilDistanceText: These distances control when a stroke closes or edits an existing path. They are measured in screen points, not millimeters.
exportText: SVG is the current export format. Exporting artwork from the main canvas requires Premium.
saveText: Set the autosave interval and iCloud preference. Check the saved project and its sync status before opening it on another device.
advancedNote: Use Apply Settings to keep your changes. Complexity, edge smoothing and rendering quality are visible controls; this guide does not make unverified claims about their effects.
generationTitle: Apply the template and inspect the puzzle
generationIntro: This example uses the Website Demo Wave slot template and a circular outline to compare the input and generated result.
generationNote: This example uses an 800 × 600 px canvas, a target of 100 pieces, Grid Size 10 and slot distances 10–50. Inspect the new group and connections, then refine or export the SVG. These screenshots demonstrate the workflow, not a speed benchmark.
iphoneIntro: Use the compact toolbar to draw, open the inspector for settings, and expand Layers to inspect the generated paths. These are actual iPhone app screens from the simulator.
